question.text: Let \(\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})=\tan ^{-1} \mathrm{x}\). Then \(\mathrm{f}^{\prime}(\mathrm{x})+\mathrm{f}^{\prime \prime}(\mathrm{x})\) is \(=0\), when \(\mathrm{x}\) is equal to

solution.text:
Hints: \(f(x)=\tan ^{-1} x\)
\(\begin{aligned}
& f^{\prime}(x)=\frac{1}{1+x^2} \\
& f^{\prime \prime}(x)=\frac{-1}{\left(1+x^2\right)} \cdot 2 x, \frac{1}{1+x^2}=\frac{2 x}{\left(1+x^2\right)^2} \\
& 1+x^2=2 x,(x-1)^2=0 \\
& x=1
\end{aligned}\)
